items.title: PCBA Manufacturing Engineer
items.description: About the Team OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. We work closely with hardware design teams, manufacturing partners, suppliers, and data center operations to deliver the compute platforms that power frontier AI. The Manufacturing Engineering team ensures our hardware can be built, tested, deployed, and supported at hyperscale. We bridge Hardware Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Contract Manufacturers, and Hardware Operations to continuously improve manufacturing performance throughout the product lifecycle. As our fleet grows globally, sustaining manufacturing engineering becomes increasingly important to maintain product quality, improve manufacturability, and rapidly resolve production issues. About the Role We are seeking a PCBA Manufacturing Engineer (Sustaining) to support production and continuous improvement of printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) used throughout Industrial Compute hardware platforms. This role focuses on sustaining engineering after product launch. You'll partner closely with Hardware Design, Quality, Manufacturing, Test Engineering, Supply Chain, and our contract manufacturers to resolve production issues, improve manufacturing yield, reduce failures, implement engineering changes, and ensure stable high-volume manufacturing. The ideal candidate has experience supporting complex server, networking, accelerator, storage, or high-performance electronics manufacturing environments. Key Responsibilities - Own sustaining manufacturing engineering for PCBA production across multiple hardware platforms. - Drive root cause investigations for manufacturing defects, field failures, and production escapes. - Partner with Hardware Design Engineers to improve manufacturability (DFM/DFA/DFT). - Support engineering change orders (ECOs) and manufacturing change implementation. - Work directly with contract manufacturers to improve production yield, cycle time, and quality. - Analyze manufacturing data to identify recurring process issues and improvement opportunities. - Develop corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) for manufacturing and supplier quality issues. - Support failure analysis activities including electrical, functional, and process investigations. - Improve manufacturing documentation, work instructions, assembly processes, and test procedures. - Collaborate with Test Engineering to improve production test coverage and manufacturing diagnostics. - Support supplier qualification, process validation, and manufacturing readiness for design revisions. - Travel to manufacturing partners as needed to support production and issue resolution. Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field. - 5+ years supporting high-volume PCBA manufacturing. - Experience with SMT manufacturing, PCB fabrication, and electronic assembly processes. - Strong understanding of manufacturing process control, yield improvement, and statistical analysis. - Experience performing root cause analysis using methodologies such as 8D, 5 Why, Fishbone, or FMEA. - Experience working with contract manufacturers and global supply chains. - Ability to interpret schematics, BOMs, assembly drawings, and manufacturing documentation. - Excellent cross-functional communication and project management skills. Preferred Skills - Experience with server, accelerator, networking, storage, or AI hardware platforms. - Familiarity with ICT, Flying Probe, Boundary Scan, Functional Test, and System-Level Test. - Experience supporting high-speed PCBAs involving GPUs, CPUs, memory, PCIe, Ethernet, or high-speed interconnects. - Knowledge of IPC standards (IPC-A-610, IPC-6012, IPC-7711/7721). - Experience with manufacturing execution systems (MES), PLM systems, and engineering change management. - Enjoy solving complex manufacturing problems using data and structured root cause analysis. - Like working directly with manufacturing partners and factory teams. - Can bridge hardware design and manufacturing execution. - Have strong troubleshooting skills across electronics, assembly processes, and production testing. - Enjoy continuous improvement and process optimization. - Are comfortable balancing technical depth with fast operational execution. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://form.asana.com/?d=57018692298241&k=5MqR40fZd7jlxVUh5J-UeA. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link https://form.asana.com/?k=bQ7w9h3iexRlicUdWRiwvg&d=57018692298241. OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy https://cdn.openai.com/policies/global-employee-and-contractor-privacy-policy.pdf At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

items.title: 社交产品负责人
items.description: 【关于公司】 我们是全球最早、最具规模的数字资产平台之一,服务全球数千万用户。作为全球排名前列的交易所之一,我们提供覆盖数千种数字资产的全套交易和财富管理产品。我们在全球主要金融中心拥有数千名员工,以远程优先、高度自主的文化运作,吸引那些在快节奏、高强度智力环境中成长的人才。我们正在构建下一代互联网的金融基础设施。 【为什么是这个岗位】 交易平台不能只靠交易工具赢得用户注意力。下一层增长来自内容、关系、社区信任，以及用户在股票、港美股、虚拟货币和 Web3 场景中的社交决策。你将主导社交产品线从早期规模走向成熟体系，把社区行为转化为拉新、日活、留存、内容消费时长和交易转化。未来 12-24 个月，你要留下一个有差异化的社交产品矩阵、一套更清晰的增长引擎，以及一支能够持续迭代的产品团队。 【你要做什么】 制定社交产品战略、定位、阶段目标和产品矩阵，覆盖主流资产交易用户与 Web3 场景 推动产品从洞察、设计到上线迭代，覆盖图文社区、用户关系、群组互动、内容分发、直播和社交交易 建立社交渗透率、日活、留存率、内容消费时长、创作者活跃和交易转化等指标体系，并用数据决定优先级 从用户研究、竞品判断和行为数据中识别真实需求，转化为提升活跃、粘性和信任的产品决策 搭建产品团队的目标、节奏和跨部门协作机制，连接增长、运营、内容、KOL、合规、安全和研发 在产品设计阶段纳入内容安全、隐私保护、数据安全和行业合规要求，避免规模化之后补漏洞 【你需要带来什么】 Non-negotiables 你完整主导过社交、社区、内容分发或增长产品，从策略制定到上线迭代，并拿到可衡量结果 你理解交易用户如何建立判断、追踪信号、消费内容、与他人互动，并把信任转化为行动 你能在用户反馈、市场变化、竞品动作、数据模式和业务目标之间提炼清晰产品方向 你带过小型产品团队，能建立协作规则，并把内容安全、隐私保护、数据安全和合规要求放进产品决策 Bonus 你做过金融科技社区、券商 App、交易平台、虚拟货币交易所、Web3 生态或社交交易产品 你熟悉内容推流、创作者生态、社区机制、群组互动、直播内容或内容驱动增长 【招聘经理寄语】 我们寻找的不是一个只会做社区功能的人，而是一个真正理解内容、关系与交易如何相互驱动的产品领导者。这个岗位需要你既能看见长期趋势，也能把复杂问题拆成可落地的产品路径。我们希望你能和团队一起，打造一个不只是让用户交易，更让用户愿意停留、互动、分享和建立信任的平台。

items.title: Machine Learning Engineer, API Multicloud
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s API Multicloud team is responsible for extending OpenAI’s API platform into strategic cloud environments, starting with AWS https://openai.com/index/openai-on-aws/. The team’s mission is to distribute OpenAI’s API broadly and safely by enabling key API technologies in AWS-native environments, in close partnership with Amazon and internal teams across Codex, Research, Safety Systems, and Applied. The team is focused on bringing core developer and enterprise capabilities into cloud-native environments, including AWS-hosted Codex, model customization / post-training as a service, and new stateful runtime environments for agentic workloads. This work sits at the intersection of production ML systems, developer platforms, model behavior, and large-scale infrastructure. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring Machine Learning Engineers to build and improve the AI systems that help strategic partners adapt OpenAI models to important use cases in cloud-native environments. This role spans post-training workflows, evaluation, data pipelines, model behavior, and API/infrastructure integration. You’ll work at the boundary between partner needs and core ML systems: helping teams understand what is and isn’t working, diagnosing issues in training and evaluation workflows, and turning those learnings into improvements to the underlying platform. You should enjoy working with external technical partners, extracting the real goal from messy requests, and pushing back or reframing when the requested experiment is not the highest-leverage path. You’ll collaborate closely with Research, Applied, Safety Systems, infrastructure teams, and external technical partners to solve ambiguous model-performance problems. When you succeed, strategic partners and internal teams will be able to improve model behavior with confidence, driving measurable product improvements while the systems behind that work become more reliable, scalable, and effective over time. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Partner with strategic customers and internal teams to define target model behaviors, diagnose failure modes, and translate real-world needs into training, evaluation, and system requirements. - Build and scale production ML systems for model customization, post-training, and fine-tuning-as-a-service workflows. - Design, run, and interpret experiments to see whether training and customization workflows are producing the intended outcomes, and identify changes to data, evaluation, training, or infrastructure that improve performance. - Partner with backend and infrastructure engineers to integrate ML capabilities into AWS-native API environments. - Feed learnings from partner deployments back into the platform by proposing and implementing improvements to post-training systems, tooling, APIs, and developer workflows. - Work closely with Research and Applied teams to bring model improvements, training workflows, and evaluation best practices into production. - Help design systems that allow strategic partners and enterprise customers to safely customize OpenAI models for high-value use cases. - Debug and improve complex systems spanning model behavior, training data, APIs, distributed infrastructure, and customer-facing product surfaces. - Operate with high ownership in a 0→1 environment where requirements are ambiguous, systems are evolving quickly, and reliability matters. YOUR BACKGROUND MIGHT LOOK SOMETHING LIKE: - Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. - 3+ years of professional engineering experience in relevant ML, infrastructure, or product-driven engineering roles. - Strong ML engineering experience building, training, fine-tuning, evaluating, or deploying production AI systems, with hands-on experience in deep learning, transformer models, and frameworks like PyTorch or TensorFlow. - Hands-on experience with training and fine-tuning large language models, including methods like supervised fine-tuning, distillation, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, or other post-training techniques. - Strong software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, systems design, and high-quality production code in Python, Rust, or similar languages. - Experience with model customization, evaluation systems, data pipelines, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, or production ML platform tradeoffs. - Ability to operate across model behavior, APIs, and infrastructure, while collaborating closely with Research, Safety, product engineering, infrastructure, and external technical partners. - Comfort moving quickly through ambiguity, owning problems end-to-end, and learning whatever is needed to get the job done. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. items.title: Strategic Sourcing Manager, Data Center Infrastructure, Electrical
items.description: About the Team OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. Working alongside leading cloud providers, engineering firms, construction partners, utilities, and equipment manufacturers, we are delivering hyperscale AI campuses that enable the next generation of frontier AI models. The Strategic Sourcing team develops and executes the commercial strategies that ensure our infrastructure programs have reliable access to the equipment, materials, and strategic partners needed to deliver at unprecedented scale. We partner closely with Infrastructure Delivery, Capacity Planning, Design Engineering, Hardware Operations, Finance, Legal, and our external suppliers to build a resilient global supply network capable of supporting Industrial Compute's long-term growth. As we continue expanding globally, strategic sourcing becomes a critical competitive advantage, ensuring our infrastructure programs remain cost-effective, resilient, and capable of executing against aggressive deployment timelines. About the Role We are seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager, Data Center Infrastructure to lead sourcing strategy for the critical infrastructure systems that power Industrial Compute campuses. This role will develop commercial strategies, negotiate strategic supplier agreements, and manage relationships across engineering, construction, manufacturing, and infrastructure partners responsible for delivering mission-critical facilities. You will work closely with Infrastructure Delivery, Capacity Planning, Engineering, Finance, Construction, and external suppliers to ensure Industrial Compute has the capacity, supplier relationships, and commercial frameworks required to support rapid global expansion. The ideal candidate has experience sourcing major infrastructure systems for hyperscale data centers, mission-critical facilities, industrial construction, semiconductor manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or similarly complex capital projects. Key Responsibilities - Develop long-term sourcing strategies for data center infrastructure systems supporting Industrial Compute. - Lead strategic supplier selection, RFx processes, commercial negotiations, and contract execution for major infrastructure programs. - Build and maintain executive relationships with key suppliers, manufacturers, EPC firms, integrators, and infrastructure vendors. - Partner with Infrastructure Delivery and Engineering to align sourcing strategies with project schedules, technical requirements, and deployment priorities. - Collaborate with Capacity Planning to ensure supplier capacity aligns with long-term infrastructure roadmaps. - Evaluate supplier capabilities across manufacturing capacity, execution quality, financial health, delivery performance, and operational maturity. - Identify and mitigate supply chain risks through supplier diversification, long-term agreements, alternative sourcing strategies, and capacity reservations. - Monitor global market conditions, manufacturing trends, commodity impacts, geopolitical risks, and supplier ecosystems that may affect infrastructure delivery. - Develop supplier scorecards and performance metrics across quality, cost, schedule, responsiveness, safety, and execution. - Support executive sourcing decisions through financial analysis, market intelligence, scenario planning, and supplier benchmarking. - Partner with Legal and Finance to structure scalable commercial agreements that support Industrial Compute's long-term infrastructure strategy. Qualifications - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Construction Management, Business, Operations, Finance, or a related field. - 8+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, supplier management, or infrastructure supply chain management. - Experience sourcing major infrastructure systems, industrial equipment, mission-critical facilities, or large capital projects. - Proven experience negotiating complex commercial agreements with strategic suppliers. - Strong understanding of supplier qualification, contract strategy, supplier performance management, and sourcing governance. - Experience partnering with engineering, construction, finance, legal, and operations organizations. - Excellent analytical, financial modeling, negotiation, and executive communication skills. items.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - Sydney
items.description: About the team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development. About the role Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) lead complex end-to-end deployments of frontier models in production alongside our most strategic customers. You will own discovery, technical scoping, system design, build, and production rollout, partnering directly with customer engineering and domain teams. You will measure success through production adoption, measurable workflow impact, and eval-driven feedback that changes product and model roadmaps. You’ll work closely with our Product, Research, Partnerships, GRC, Security, and GTM teams. This role is based in Sydney. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required. In this role you will - Own technical delivery across multiple deployments from first prototype to stable production. - Build full-stack systems that deliver customer value and sharpen how we learn. - Embed closely with customer teams, understand their needs, and guide adoption of what you build. - Scope work, sequence delivery, and remove blockers early. - Make trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality; adjust plans to protect delivery. - Contribute directly in the code when progress or clarity depends on it. - Codify working patterns into tools, playbooks, or building blocks that others can use. - Share field feedback that helps Research and Product understand where the models succeed and where they can improve. - Keep teams moving through clarity and follow-through. You might thrive in this role if you - Bring 5+ years of engineering or technical deployment experience that includes customer-facing work. - Have scoped and delivered complex systems in fast-moving or ambiguous environments. - Write and review production-grade code across frontend and backend using Python, JavaScript, or comparable stacks. - Have built or deployed systems powered by LLMs or generative models and understand how model behaviour affects product experience. - Simplify complexity and make fast, sound decisions under pressure. - Communicate clearly with engineers, product teams, and customer stakeholders. - Spot risks early and adjust without slowing down. - Model calm and judgment when the stakes are high. items.title: Partner Director, McKinsey Alliance
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic, global partner ecosystem designed to accelerate customer success, enable enterprise AI adoption, and drive durable growth in support of OpenAI’s mission. We work closely across Product, Research, Sales, Legal, Communications, and regional leadership to ensure a cohesive strategy and disciplined execution with our most strategic partners. ABOUT THE ROLE We are hiring a Partner Director, Global McKinsey Alliance to lead and scale OpenAI’s relationship with McKinsey & Company. This role will serve as the single accountable executive owner of the alliance globally. You will define the partnership strategy and operating model, translating executive alignment into scaled commercial and transformation outcomes across regions and industries. You will work closely with McKinsey’s global leadership, industry and functional practices, and technology organizations—including QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey—to develop differentiated enterprise AI offerings, pursue complex transformation opportunities, and help customers move from strategy to production deployment and measurable value. The role carries responsibility for the health, performance, and long-term expansion of the partnership. Success requires senior executive presence, sound judgment, commercial discipline, technical fluency, and the ability to operate effectively across a complex, partner-led organization. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Own the global McKinsey relationship, including alliance strategy, pipeline growth, enterprise impact, deployment scale, and long-term expansion across priority industries. - Define and run the partnership’s operating model across executive governance, joint planning, regional execution, opportunity management, resource allocation, and escalation. - Serve as OpenAI’s senior executive counterpart to McKinsey’s global leadership and relevant industry, functional, technology, and regional leaders. - Develop a differentiated alliance strategy that combines McKinsey’s strategy, industry expertise, transformation capabilities, and executive relationships with OpenAI’s research, models, products, and technical expertise. - Build a deep working relationship with QuantumBlack and other McKinsey technology and AI teams to develop repeatable solutions and move customer programs from strategy and experimentation into production. - Set joint priorities, establish clear ownership, resolve escalations, and coordinate execution across global and regional teams. - Shape and lead the co-selling of complex, CxO- and board-level enterprise AI transformation opportunities. - Engage directly with enterprise executives alongside McKinsey leaders to frame AI strategy, operating models, use-case portfolios, governance, adoption plans, organizational change, and value realization. - Identify priority industries, transformation plays, and lighthouse accounts where the partnership can create differentiated and repeatable customer value. - Coordinate OpenAI stakeholders across Product, Research, Sales, Solutions Architecture, Technical Success, Legal, Finance, Communications, and Operations to support strategic pursuits and deployments. - Establish clear rules of engagement and guardrails for intellectual property, solution quality, safety, delivery, commercial ownership, and customer accountability. - Build McKinsey’s capability to position, design, and deliver solutions powered by OpenAI through executive alignment, technical enablement, solution patterns, readiness programs, and disciplined delivery handoffs. - Develop joint assets and offerings that can scale beyond individual engagements while maintaining the rigor required for highly strategic customers. - Allocate OpenAI resources based on strategic value, revenue potential, customer impact, repeatability, delivery readiness, and partner performance. - Build and lead a dedicated alliance pod over time, spanning partner management, technical leadership, enablement, and operations. - Establish durable reporting, metrics, and operating cadences covering pipeline, conversion, production adoption, customer outcomes, partner readiness, delivery quality, and return on OpenAI investment. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE: - Partner, Senior Partner, Managing Director, or equivalent senior leadership experience at McKinsey, another leading strategy firm, or a top-tier technology or transformation organization. - A strong combination of technology fluency and commercial leadership across business development, enterprise transformation, industry advisory, GTM, or strategic alliances. - Proven ownership of a global, multi-year strategic partnership with executive accountability and measurable commercial and customer outcomes. - Demonstrated success shaping and closing high-stakes, board-level transformation opportunities and moving them from strategy through production deployment. - Experience designing and scaling operating models between senior, partner-led organizations, including governance, incentives, account planning, staffing, delivery handoffs, and escalation. - Credibility with senior leaders in strategy consulting and enterprise technology, with a practical understanding of partnership economics, regional structures, and decision-making networks. - Strong executive presence and the judgment to make tradeoffs, resolve conflict, and maintain momentum under ambiguity and scrutiny. - The ability to influence Product, Research, Sales, Technical, Legal, Finance, Communications, and partner organizations without relying on direct authority. - Deep literacy in enterprise AI, data, cloud, security, governance, and organizational transformation, with credibility among CEOs, CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, and other senior executives. - Experience working with data science, AI engineering, or advanced analytics organizations such as QuantumBlack or comparable groups. - Industry expertise in at least one priority vertical, such as financial services, healthcare, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, retail and consumer, technology, industrials, or energy. - Experience building repeatable solutions or transformation plays from high-value strategic engagements. - A disciplined approach to portfolio management, including deciding when to invest, scale, redirect, or decline an opportunity. - Preferably, experience with private-equity value creation, portfolio transformation, capability building, or large-scale operating-model change. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: - OpenAI and McKinsey have a clear alliance thesis, differentiated value proposition, executive governance model, and measurable joint plan. - The partnership generates qualified, strategically aligned pipeline and converts priority opportunities into production deployments with demonstrable customer value. - McKinsey teams can confidently identify, position, design, and support enterprise transformations powered by OpenAI. - The relationship with QuantumBlack and other McKinsey technology teams produces strong technical collaboration, repeatable solution patterns, and disciplined paths from prototype to production. - OpenAI resources are allocated transparently and concentrated on opportunities with the greatest strategic, commercial, customer, and repeatable impact. - Joint assets and transformation approaches move beyond bespoke engagements into reusable, industry-relevant offerings. - OpenAI’s field understands when and how to engage McKinsey, and McKinsey teams understand OpenAI’s standards, guardrails, resources, and escalation paths. - The alliance demonstrates sustained executive sponsorship, high-quality delivery, partner accountability, production adoption, and year-over-year growth. You'll work closely with IT Engineering and Security, with opportunities to grow into more technical infrastructure work over time. Responsibilities End-User Support Triage and resolve issues across hardware, software, networking, and accounts — primarily through our ticketing system, with additional support via Slack and in-person Diagnose and resolve issues across macOS, ChromeOS, iOS, Android, and our core SaaS platforms (Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, Atlassian) Troubleshoot device issues, including enrollment, configuration profiles, and policy enforcement Support access management and employee lifecycle workflows (onboarding, offboarding, reorgs) Handle escalations requiring cross-team coordination Participate in an on-call rotation for urgent issues outside business hours Provide hands-on support for user technology, AV systems, conference rooms, and printers Communication & Documentation Communicate clearly with users of all technical levels Write and maintain internal documentation including runbooks, how-to guides, and knowledge base articles Identify patterns in support requests, surface recurring issues to the team, and identify opportunities for automation or systemic solves Operational Improvement Help streamline onboarding and other high-volume operations as the company scales Contribute to automation efforts Maintain and improve device management, identity, and access systems Assist with scripting (Bash, Python) to automate repetitive tasks You may be a good fit if you Have 7+ years of hands-on IT support experience, ideally in a fast-paced or high-growth environment Are an excellent communicator who genuinely enjoys helping people solve problems Have strong troubleshooting skills and are methodical, curious, and persistent Demonstrated experience supporting macOS endpoints and comfortable supporting ChromeOS, iOS, and Android Have significant experience with Google Workspace administration Have experience with Slack administration — workspace management, permissions, and troubleshooting Have substantial experience supporting and administering additional SaaS tools Understand identity and access fundamentals — SSO, MFA, directory services Are familiar with MDM fundamentals and endpoint management concepts Have experience with basic scripting (Bash or Python) for automation Take ownership of problems and follow through until they're resolved Think beyond the immediate fix — you ask "why did this happen?" and "how do we prevent it?" Are organized enough to manage competing priorities without things falling through the cracks Propose solutions when you see a process that doesn't scale Are looking to develop deeper technical skills and take on more complex systems administration challenges over time Strong candidates may also Be familiar with zero-trust security concepts and endpoint security tooling Have experience with networking basics — DNS, DHCP, VPNs, networking fundamentals Have contributed to IT projects beyond day-to-day support (migrations, tool rollouts, process redesigns) Have experience using AI tools to improve personal or team productivity Location This role is based in our San Francisco, Seattle, New York or Washington DC office and there is a 4 day/week in office expectation. items.title: Senior Data Scientist / Analyst, Institutional
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's fastest growing prediction market. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future. We're growing fast, both in terms of volume ($115B traded to date) and adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media and we need your help adding fuel to the fire. ABOUT THE ROLE Polymarket is looking for a Senior Data Scientist / Analyst to own the analytics behind our institutional relationships — the market makers, large takers, and brokerages that account for a disproportionate share of platform volume. You'll be the person who understands each of these counterparties in depth: how they trade, how they make money with us, and whether the relationship is getting healthier or weaker. This is a role for someone comfortable on both sides of the conversation — rigorous enough to analyze flow at the order level, and commercial enough to sit in a partner review and explain what the numbers mean for the terms of the relationship. And you'll do it in a fast-moving environment where the institutional side of the business is being built as you go. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the analytics on our largest makers, takers, and brokerages, and be the internal source of truth on how each relationship is performing - Build the account-level view of every major counterparty — volume, flow composition, spread capture, fee and rebate economics, and how each has trended over time - Monitor counterparty health and surface concentration risk, deteriorating engagement, or churn signals early enough for the team to act on them - Analyze trading behavior to understand how each participant actually makes money on our platform, and whether the terms we have given them still make sense - Support the institutional team through reviews and negotiations with the analysis behind them — what a counterparty is worth, what they are asking for, and what we should be willing to give - Quantify how institutional flow affects the broader market, including liquidity, spreads, and the experience of retail traders on the other side of it - Work with analytics engineers to turn recurring relationship reporting into modeled datasets, so account reviews do not start from scratch every quarter - Own documentation end-to-end — writing clearly and thoroughly enough that anyone on the team can pick up your analysis without friction WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 7+ years in analytics, trading, or counterparty analysis, ideally at an exchange, trading venue, brokerage, or market making firm - Expert SQL — you can work directly against order book and transaction-level data without supervision - Deep understanding of how professional participants make money — spread capture, adverse selection, inventory risk, and the economics of providing liquidity - Credibility in a technical conversation with a sophisticated counterparty — you can hold your own with a firm's own quants - Commercial instinct — you can look at a relationship and articulate what it is worth to us and where the leverage sits - Strong communication and discretion, including with sensitive counterparty information and in front of external partners - Comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where business logic changes frequently and you need to keep pace - (Plus) Experience with institutional pricing, fee tiers, or rebate program design - (Plus) Familiarity with on-chain data or blockchain analytics - (Plus) Python or R for deeper statistical work on trading behavior - (Plus) Experience in fintech, crypto, prediction markets, or other data-intensive financial products BENEFITS - Competitive salary & equity - Unlimited PTO - Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage - 401k match - Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $200,000 to $300,000 annually, plus equity and benefits. This range reflects a good-faith estimate for this position. Experience levels vary widely within a title here, so please reach out even if your expectations fall outside it. We're always happy to chat.

It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. 30M+ customers and 500+ ecosystem partners run on us. Licensed in the U.S. Regulated across the UK, EU, Canada, and Australia. AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters. You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together. The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building for what's next, for humans and agents. Recent recognition: Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 . 2nd in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100 The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. This is a high-impact, highly cross-functional role at the intersection of strategy, business operations, and corporate development. You will act as a force multiplier for the SVP, helping translate strategic priorities into clear plans, driving complex initiatives forward, and ensuring alignment and accountability across teams. You’ll work across a broad range of topics, from supporting strategic transactions and partnerships to improving operating cadence and tackling high-priority projects that don’t sit neatly within a single team. The ideal candidate combines strong strategic judgment with an operator mindset: someone who can move seamlessly from structuring an ambiguous problem to getting into the details required to deliver an outcome. 2. Lead high-priority strategic and cross-functional initiatives from definition through execution, bringing structure and momentum to complex or ambiguous problems. Support corporate development priorities, including strategic transactions, partnerships, investments, and other opportunities that accelerate MoonPay’s growth. Drive alignment across senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams, identifying dependencies, resolving blockers, and ensuring critical decisions and actions move forward. Build and continuously improve operating cadences, including prioritisation, planning, decision-making processes, and tracking against key objectives. Develop high-quality strategic analysis and materials that synthesize complex information, surface key trade-offs, and enable senior leadership to make informed decisions. 3. items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Senior Engineering Manager for Payment Platform within the Platform group, you'll lead the engineering organization responsible for orchestrating the payment flow and the network connecting Coinbase to the global financial system. Payment Platform owns the infrastructure that bridges traditional finance and crypto — on-ramp and off-ramp processing, bank and card network integrations, and stablecoin settlement — spanning fiat and crypto rails across financial institutions worldwide. You'll build and scale multiple engineering teams, set the technical vision for Payment Platform integration and settlement systems, and partner with Product, Finance, Compliance, and Engineering leadership to drive the multi-quarter roadmap for how money moves in and out of Coinbase. What you’ll do: Build, scale, and lead a multi-team engineering organization across Payment Platform, managing engineering managers and senior ICs while coaching the org on technical excellence and career development Define the technical vision and architectural strategy for Payment Platform infrastructure, driving decisions on bank/card network connectivity, stablecoin settlement, reconciliation, and failover across a large and growing set of financial institution partners Partner with Product, Finance, Compliance, and Engineering leadership to shape and execute the multi-quarter roadmap, translating regulatory constraints and partner-integration complexity into iterative, shippable milestones Own engineering quality and operational excellence across Payment Platform, including SLA accountability, incident response, and the engineering standards that ensure funds move correctly and on time at scale Drive talent strategy for the Payment Platform engineering org, partnering with recruiting to identify exceptional engineers with payments/fintech infrastructure depth and developing the next generation of engineering leaders within the team Required Skills and Experience: 10+ years in software engineering with 5+ years of engineering management experience, including 2+ years managing managers and scaling multi-team engineering organizations Proven track record delivering and operating distributed payment systems, financial infrastructure, or high-volume transactional platforms at scale, with deep understanding of rails such as ACH, cards, SEPA, or wire transfers Strong technical judgment with demonstrated ability to guide architecture, reliability, and engineering quality for critical financial services, including hands-on operational leadership through incidents and service health management Experience setting strategy and delivering complex work through multiple teams in regulated environments, partnering closely with Risk, Compliance, Finance, and Operations to balance speed, safety, and regulatory requirements Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). Total compensation may also include equity and bonus eligibility, and benefits (medical, dental, vision, 401(k)). Annual base salary range (excluding equity and bonus): $253,895 — $298,700 USD Application Limit: Candidates may submit a maximum of 3 applications within a 6-month period. Equal Opportunity Employer: Coinbase is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information. Applicants with criminal histories will be considered consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. US Applicants: View Employee Rights , Know Your Rights , and E-Verify Notice of Participation. Accommodations: If you are an individual with a disability who needs a reasonable accommodation, email us your request and contact info at accommodations[at]coinbase.com. Need screen reading technology? Click here to download a free compatible screen reader and view the tutorial . Data Privacy & Arbitration: By submitting your application, you agree to our Candidate Privacy Notice . US applicants: By submitting your application, you agree to Arbitration of Disputes .

items.description: Perplexity is looking for a frontend engineer to build the design system behind every Perplexity product. It is the component library and design language shared across web, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows – the primitives, tokens, and interaction patterns that every product team builds on top of. Its users are internal, spanning product teams and a broad range of contributors across the company. The components you build become the foundation all of them rely on. You will develop component APIs that hold up across dozens of consuming surfaces and are easy for other teams to adopt correctly, contribute to the token pipeline that keeps five platforms visually consistent, and maintain a high bar for interaction quality and accessibility. Tech Stack: React · TypeScript · CSS · Design Tokens WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design and build core primitives – overlays, inputs, navigation, feedback – with APIs that stay coherent as consumers multiply - Work across the design-token pipeline – authoring, generation, and per-platform publishing across web, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows - Partner directly with design on the design language itself, translating Figma systems into typed, testable, documented components - Migrate product surfaces off bespoke implementations onto shared primitives without breaking them - Build accessible components by default – keyboard, focus, contrast, screen readers – backed by automated coverage - Support consuming teams through docs, visual regression coverage, and on-call rotation WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 4+ years building production frontend; experience with a design system, component library, or shared UI platform is a plus - Interest in building reusable components - Strong React and TypeScript, and CSS - Working accessibility knowledge (WCAG, ARIA patterns, assistive tech) - Comfort collaborating closely with designers on the visual and interaction language

items.title: Product Manager, New Markets and Monetization
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's New Markets and Monetization team exists to bring transformational AI to every business. Model capabilities are compounding, and the Claude Platform is how businesses build with our models. Our job within the Claude Platform is to make sure that every industry, not just software, can build on frontier AI with our APIs and that everyone who builds on Claude prospers by it. The work falls into two pillars that reinforce each other. Verticals: identifying and building for the next API markets. Monetization: the commercial machinery that lets the platform do business anywhere, with anyone: a single way for usage that flows through partners, resellers, and other platforms. We're hiring the founding product managers onto this team, and this posting covers all of them. You will own one of the areas below outright, work day to day with a dedicated engineering lead and designer, and be measured on numbers that are company-level goals for the half. Almost none of this exists yet, so most weeks you will be the person defining the problem rather than receiving it. Key responsibilities Partner and platform billing. How usage that reaches Claude through a partner, reseller, or another platform is metered, attributed, and billed, and the program terms that go with it, so indirect volume can grow without our risk growing with it. Spend observability and controls. Giving enterprise buyers a precise view of what they spend and where, and turning that into limits and controls they can enforce, including programmatically. One account, and the startup path built on it. One login and one wallet across the API and Claude's subscriptions, so a builder's first commit, first production call, and first invoice are on a single plan. A vertical. The platform strategy for a particular industry: what builders there need that the platform doesn't yet do, which bets to make, and shipping them with the vertical's own product and go-to-market partners. Whatever your focus, you will: Build on primitives owned by the Billing Platform and Auth & Identity teams, and ship with Growth, Go-to-Market and Startups, Legal, Finance, and Data Science Structure the commercial terms yourself, whether that's pricing, revenue attribution, or partner and startup program terms, with Finance, Legal, and Business Development Talk to every side of the ecosystem, from enterprise buyers and startup builders to the partners that resell or embed Claude and the industry customers we're building for, and turn it into a roadmap where each new participant makes the platform more valuable to the rest Own the team's outcome metrics: the share of the platform's business outside coding, new startup revenue, volume unified across the API and Claude's subscriptions, and the volume partners book on Claude, and make sure the instrumentation exists to know whether what you shipped moved them Write the strategy, the specs, and the analysis yourself Minimum qualifications Have owned a developer platform, API, billing or money-movement product, or self-serve growth product end to end, and were the person accountable for its revenue or activation number (for most people this means five or more years as a PM, but we care about the ownership, not the years) Have built with or shipped on top of large language models, and have a view on what changes about billing, identity, or distribution when the customer is sometimes an agent Are technically fluent: you read API docs, work through a billing, identity, or attribution design with engineers, and make calls on platform primitives yourself Pull your own data: SQL or equivalent, to define a metric, build a funnel, or size a market Have negotiated pricing, revenue share, or program terms with Finance, Legal, or Business Development counterparts Write clearly enough that an engineer, an executive, and an external partner can each see the tradeoff you're making Care about Anthropic's mission, and specifically about growing this platform in a way where the people building on it share in the upside Preferred qualifications 8+ years of product management experience Worked on metering, usage attribution, reseller or cloud-marketplace channels, or enterprise spend management Taken a developer platform into a new industry, or built product in healthcare, life sciences, financial services, or another regulated industry Grown a developer product's self-serve or startup business, including its pricing and packaging Built account, identity, or subscription systems that span more than one product Taken a product from zero to one, where the users, the product, and the economics all had to be worked out at once The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: Specialist, CSIRT
items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Security Operations Specialist on the Security Operations team, you'll defend Coinbase and its customers against some of the most sophisticated attackers in the world. This team - spanning CDRE, Insider Threat, Blockops and Threat Intelligence - protects billions of dollars in digital assets while scaling security coverage for the next billion crypto users. You'll own frontline incident response, build detection and automation capabilities, and partner across the organization to keep Coinbase safe as it launches new Web3 products globally. What you'll do: Own second-line triage and response for security alerts, leading incident management through resolution and driving post-incident improvements Build and maintain runbooks for repeatable response patterns, then define and implement automation to eliminate manual toil Partner with teams across Security Operations to develop monitoring strategies informed by attacker investigation findings Drive Security monitoring and incident response for emerging Web3 product launches Strengthen team capabilities by mentoring peers, sharing knowledge, and participating in 24/7 rotational coverage across time zones Required Skills and Experience: 3+ years of hands-on security operations experience including incident response, alert triage, and network/host forensics across cloud, SaaS, and container environments Demonstrated ability to identify detection gaps and build coverage across diverse log sources (cloud platforms, SaaS applications, container orchestration, M&A integrations) Proficiency scripting automation workflows that reduce manual investigation and response time (Python, Bash, or equivalent) Working knowledge of networking fundamentals and operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS) sufficient to analyze host and network-level artifacts Experience working with SIEM platforms and threat intelligence tooling at scale, including tuning alerts and improving signal-to-noise ratios Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. items.title: Backend Software Engineer - Codex for Finance
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI for Financial Services is part of OpenAI's Verticals organization, which focuses on accelerating the economy and knowledge work. We build AI products for financial institutions and the professionals who power them, from investment bankers and research analysts to investors and other financial services teams. We combine OpenAI's models, financial data, and enterprise knowledge to help professionals research companies, analyze markets, and produce high-quality work in the tools they use every day. We're a small, entrepreneurial team working closely with customers and partners across research, product, design, engineering, and go-to-market to bring new capabilities from idea to production. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for backend engineers to build the systems that make advanced AI useful, reliable, and trustworthy in financial services. You'll build the data systems, agentic workflows, and enterprise integrations behind our products. You'll also help bring them into production at some of the world's largest financial institutions. items.title: Compute Country Lead, Canada
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is scaling compute internationally — growing our footprint in new countries. We're hiring a Country Lead to be the single, accountable owner of our compute strategy in Canada: the person who leads a team of cross-functional experts driving site selection, leasing, energy, financing, government relations and policy, community engagement, construction, and operations. This person will be ultimately responsible for bringing gigawatts of compute online in Canada. You won't build this alone. The specialist functions — leasing, energy, policy, construction, finance — are hired and managed centrally by functional leads based in San Francisco. Your job is to provide cross-functional leadership over that team in-country: coordinating and driving accountability across workstreams, while representing Anthropic externally with government and industry counterparts in Canada. This is a high-ambiguity, high-trust role for someone who can bring structure to a fast-growing, cross-functional effort without needing formal authority to do it. Responsibilities Own the end-to-end strategy and coordination for Anthropic's compute build-out in Canada, from initial site selection through construction and operations. While each component will be run by subject matter experts, this role will act as the overall leader and coordinator of that team. Serve as the primary point of accountability for cross-functional workstreams; leasing, financing, energy, government relations/policy, community engagement, construction, and operations. Provide working leadership to the in-country cross-functional team, driving alignment and unblocking issues. Represent Anthropic with government officials, utilities, energy providers, and other external stakeholders in Canada. Build and maintain relationships within the Canadian government and the energy industry to support site, power, and policy outcomes. Track progress and surface risks across parallel workstreams as the country's compute footprint scales from initial sites to multiple gigawatts. Translate between Anthropic's global compute priorities and the specific regulatory, political, and market conditions in Canada. Requirements Canadian national with established links into government and the energy industry strongly preferred. Structured thinker with a track record of learning new domains quickly and going deep fast. Excellent communicator, comfortable representing Anthropic to senior government, utility, and industry stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to lead and coordinate cross-functional teams without direct line authority. Hyper-organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to own multiple concurrent workstreams at once. Comfortable with ambiguity; a problem solver who drives structure into undefined situations. Background in energy, infrastructure, or a related sector. Nice to have Prior experience with large-scale infrastructure or datacenter development. Existing relationships with Canadian federal or provincial government bodies relevant to energy, land use, or industrial development. Experience managing or overseeing capital-intensive projects. Familiarity with the compute, cloud, or datacenter industry. Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: Compute Country Lead, Korea
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is scaling compute internationally — growing our footprint in new countries. We're hiring a Country Lead to be the single, accountable owner of our compute strategy in Korea: the person who leads a team of cross-functional experts driving site selection, leasing, energy, financing, government relations and policy, community engagement, construction, and operations. This person will be ultimately responsible for bringing gigawatts of compute online in Korea. You won't build this alone. The specialist functions — leasing, energy, policy, construction, finance — are hired and managed centrally by functional leads based in San Francisco. Your job is to provide cross-functional leadership over that team in-country: coordinating and driving accountability across workstreams, while representing Anthropic externally with government and industry counterparts in Korea. This is a high-ambiguity, high-trust role for someone who can bring structure to a fast-growing, cross-functional effort without needing formal authority to do it. Responsibilities Own the end-to-end strategy and coordination for Anthropic's compute build-out in Korea, from initial site selection through construction and operations. While each component will be run by subject matter experts, this role will act as the overall leader and coordinator of that team. Serve as the primary point of accountability for cross-functional workstreams; leasing, financing, energy, government relations/policy, community engagement, construction, and operations. Provide working leadership to the in-country cross-functional team, driving alignment and unblocking issues. Represent Anthropic with government officials, utilities, energy providers, and other external stakeholders in Korea. Build and maintain relationships within the Korean government and the energy industry to support site, power, and policy outcomes. Track progress and surface risks across parallel workstreams as the country's compute footprint scales from initial sites to multiple gigawatts. Translate between Anthropic's global compute priorities and the specific regulatory, political, and market conditions in Korea. Requirements Korean national with established links into government and the energy industry strongly preferred. Structured thinker with a track record of learning new domains quickly and going deep fast. Excellent communicator, comfortable representing Anthropic to senior government, utility, and industry stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to lead and coordinate cross-functional teams without direct line authority. Hyper-organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to own multiple concurrent workstreams at once. Comfortable with ambiguity; a problem solver who drives structure into undefined situations. Background in energy, infrastructure, or a related sector. Nice to have Prior experience with large-scale infrastructure or datacenter development. Existing relationships with Korean federal or provincial government bodies relevant to energy, land use, or industrial development. Experience managing or overseeing capital-intensive projects. Familiarity with the compute, cloud, or datacenter industry. Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.description: Fireblocks is the company bringing global finance onchain. Backed by over $1 billion in capital, we are the premier digital asset infrastructure provider trusted by thousands of industry-defining financial institutions, including banks, payment providers, fintechs, and global corporates such as BNY Mellon, BNP Paribas, ANZ Bank, Western Union, Stripe, and Revolut. Built for institutional scale and security, our enterprise-grade platform and network have powered over $14 trillion in digital asset transfers worldwide. Solution Architect, UAE Welcome to Fireblocks, the industry-leading digital asset infrastructure technology company responsible for 15% of all crypto transactions! Here’s the bit about us: Fireblocks is an enterprise-grade platform for securely moving, storing, and issuing digital assets, powered by the Fireblocks Network and MPC-based wallet infrastructure. As of January 2026 we serve over 2,400 institutional customers, have secured over $10 trillion in digital asset transfers, and are the world’s highest-valued digital asset infrastructure company, with over $1 billion raised. Our mission is simple: enable every business to easily and securely support digital assets & cryptocurrencies. Come join us as we Secure. Simplify. Scale Here’s the bit about the opportunity: As a Solution Architect in our EMEA Professional Services team, you own the technical delivery of Fireblocks implementations for the ME region’s largest Banks and Financial Institutions. From deal close through to production, you lead architecture design, integration, and deployment on customer infrastructure. You also bring that delivery expertise into strategic pre-sales cycles, helping Sales win the deals you will go on to deliver. You’ll be: Owning the transition from deal close to production, taking end-to-end accountability for the solutions delivered Defining enterprise customers’ setup with Fireblocks, including API integrations, security architecture, and architecture documentation Steering complex integrations across core banking, custody, tokenisation, and Travel Rule through to production Codifying reusable reference architectures, integration patterns, and playbooks to scale delivery across the Middle East Acting as the bridge between Sales, Product, R&D, and customers to solve complex integration challenges Supporting strategic pre-sales cycles with technical discovery and solution design Ensuring operational excellence and a high standard of customer satisfaction throughout delivery What we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree or above in Computer Science or a related field, with 5+ years of relevant experience Proven experience delivering post-sale implementations in complex enterprise or financial services environments Experience with either blockchain, cryptography, or Web3 technologies, or with Banks, Financial Institutions, or enterprise financial systems. One is a must, both is a strong advantage Software development experience and a hands-on technical mindset Deep understanding of IT security and proven cloud experience Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture and best practices Demonstrated technical leadership, mentoring engineers or architects and setting technical standards Pre-sales exposure (solution architecture, sales engineering, or RFP support) is a plus Excellent written and spoken English with Arabic being desirable. Fireblocks' mission is to enable every business to easily and securely access digital assets and cryptocurrencies. In order to do that, we strongly believe our workforce should be as diverse as our clients, and this is why we embrace diversity and inclusion in all its forms. Please see our candidate privacy policy here .
